items.note: The page sets up the radix-2^b digits with q=ceil(n/b), counts the product degree, chains 2q-2<2n/b<=T/2<S to rule out wraparound modulo x^S-1, and bounds c_j<2^{3b}. This matches the paper's subsection 'The radix-digit polynomials' (lines 4181-4193), with the parameters b, T, S stated as in lines 4055-4058 and 4145.

It writes u=sum u_i 2^{bi}, v=sum v_k 2^{bk} with 0<=u_i,v_k<2^b and q digits ('padding with leading zeros'), and says 'Each digit polynomial has degree at most q-1, so the product polynomial has degree at most 2q-2', as the paper does.

Each link is justified: 'q<n/b+1 and so 2q-2<2n/b', '2n/b<=T/2 because T>=4n/b', and T/2<S (the paper's line 4145). It then explains that reducing modulo x^S-1 folds x^j onto x^{j mod S}, so 'nothing folds' when j<=2q-2<S. This is the paper's reasoning, written out.

'Each c_j is a sum of at most q products u_iv_k, each between 0 and (2^b-1)^2', which gives c_j<=q(2^b-1)^2, and 'Since q<=n<=2^b, this is below 2^b*2^{2b}=2^{3b}'. This is the paper's inequality (eq:capacity) with the paper's justification.
